candidates.title: Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline Efficacy for LLM-Generated Network Configurations
candidates.research_question: Does an iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline that combines LLM generation with deterministic network verification and bounded repair iterations reduce semantic/execution failures of generated device configurations compared with ungated LLM generation?
hypotheses: An iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline will produce a higher proportion of emulator-executable configurations (fewer semantic/execution failures) than ungated LLM outputs.
Most remaining execution failures after repair will be attributable to emulator-modeling gaps (device-specific runtime side effects) rather than purely syntactic or simple logical errors.
A small number of repair iterations (≤3) will capture the majority of correctable verifier-detected faults, yielding diminishing returns thereafter.
candidates.proposed_design: Curate n=200 natural-language change intents varying in scope (single-device to cross-device, ACLs, route changes). For each intent, generate an initial configuration using a fixed LLM prompt. Run a deterministic verifier (reachability/ACL checks) on the generated config. If the verifier fails, invoke an LLM-guided repair up to three iterations, re-verifying after each repair. Compare against a baseline arm of ungated LLM outputs (no verifier or repair). Emulate accepted configurations in a high-fidelity network emulator (open-source emulator configured with vendor-like CLIs). Record verifier outcomes, number of repairs, and emulator execution outcomes. Predefine inclusion/exclusion, random seeds, repair stopping rules, and safety cutoffs; preregister the plan and keep seeds/logs immutable.
candidates.expected_data: Per-intent records: intent text, initial LLM output, verifier results per iteration, repaired outputs per iteration, number of repairs applied, final verifier status, emulator deployment logs, executed CLI lines, final reachability/ACL matrices, execution error traces, time-to-accept, and metadata (devices touched, lines changed). Aggregate counts of verifier-failures corrected, uncorrectable failures, and emulator-execution failures.
candidates.primary_outcome: Emulator-executable configuration success rate (fraction of intents whose final configuration executes in the emulator without causing reachability/ACL violations) comparing generate–verify–repair pipeline vs ungated baseline.
candidates.analysis_outline: Compare success proportions between pipeline and baseline using two-proportion z-test with 95% CIs; report absolute and relative risk reductions. Use paired analyses for intents where both arms produce outputs (McNemar test). Fit logistic regression predicting emulator success with predictors: initial verifier fail (yes/no), number of devices touched, repair iterations, and config size. Report repair iteration yield curve and analyze failure taxonomy for uncorrected cases (manual root-cause coding). Report exact counts, uncertainties, and null/negative results.
risks: Emulator fidelity may not capture certain vendor runtime behaviours, biasing success upward.
Repair iterations guided by the same LLM could converge on plausibly consistent but semantically incorrect fixes (confirmation bias).
Bounded repair may hide deeper systemic errors (e.g., interactions across devices) not correctable within iteration limit.

candidates.title: Rollback Script Reliability under Verifier-Gated vs Ungated Deployment
candidates.research_question: How does verifier-gated deployment influence the effectiveness of LLM-generated rollback scripts in restoring pre-change reachability and ACL semantics when deployed changes fail?
hypotheses: Verifier-gated deployments will yield higher rollback success rates (fraction of invoked rollbacks that fully restore baseline reachability/ACL semantics) than ungated deployments because verifier gating prevents syntactically/semantically unsafe deployments.
Rollback script failures will correlate positively with change size (lines/devices touched) and with syntactic/semantic omissions not detectable by surface-level filters.
A nontrivial fraction of rollback failures will be due to emulator-modeling or side-effect timing issues (BGP convergence, transient state) rather than purely incorrect rollback commands.
candidates.proposed_design: Create n=200 change-intent tasks varying in risk and size. For each, instruct the LLM to produce (a) a deployment script and (b) a rollback script. Randomly assign tasks to two arms: (1) verifier-gated deployment (deployment permitted only if pre-deployment verifier passes) and (2) ungated deployment. For a prespecified fraction (40%) of tasks, induce a controlled failure condition during deployment (e.g., malformed ACL entry, route leak scenario) to trigger rollback invocation. Execute deployments and rollbacks in the emulator; record whether rollback scripts execute syntactically, whether they restore the prerechange reachability/ACL matrix, outage duration, and root-cause notes. Preregister rollback success definition, safety limits, retry policy, and random seeds.
candidates.expected_data: Per-change records: intent, generated deployment script, generated rollback script, pre-deploy verifier outcome, whether rollback was invoked, rollback execution logs, final reachability/ACL matrices, outage duration, change-size metrics (lines, devices touched), syntactic validity flags, and root-cause annotations for rollback failures.
candidates.primary_outcome: Rollback success rate: fraction of invoked rollbacks that fully restore baseline reachability/ACL semantics, compared between verifier-gated and ungated arms.
candidates.analysis_outline: Compare rollback-success proportions with two-proportion z-test or Fisher's exact test and report 95% CIs. Compare outage durations between arms with Mann–Whitney U test. Fit logistic regression for rollback failure with predictors: change size, devices touched, verifier pass/fail, syntactic validity of rollback script, and whether failure was induced. Conduct exploratory root-cause taxonomy for failed rollbacks and report representative failure transcripts.
risks: Emulator snapshot/restore fidelity may not reflect production stateful behaviours, biasing rollback success upward.
LLM-generated rollback scripts might omit side-effects (e.g., BGP withdraw timing) not modeled in emulator.
Ungated deployments could create destructive emulator conditions; enforce strict emulator-only execution and safety cutoffs.

candidates.title: Adversarial Prompt Robustness and Verifier+Policy Guarding in NetOps Pipelines
candidates.research_question: How susceptible are LLM-driven NetOps pipelines to adversarial/jailbreak prompts that induce unsafe configurations, and how effective is a deterministic verifier+policy-based guarded-execution pipeline at blocking these unsafe outputs prior to deployment?
hypotheses: Adversarially crafted prompts adapted to NetOps contexts will induce unsafe configuration outputs at a higher rate than benign operational prompts.

A verifier+policy gated pipeline will block a majority of adversarially-induced unsafe outputs prior to deployment, substantially reducing emulator-observed unsafe deployments relative to no mitigation.
Some adversarial outputs will bypass simple syntactic/policy filters but be caught by deeper semantics-aware deterministic verification (reachability/policy violations).
candidates.proposed_design: Curate two prompt corpora (n=150 benign operational intents; n=150 adversarial/jailbreak-style prompts constructed following documented jailbreak techniques adapted for NetOps). For each prompt, collect LLM outputs under three mitigation conditions: (1) no mitigation, (2) syntax/policy filter, (3) verifier+policy gated execution. For outputs accepted under each condition, emulate deployment to confirm unsafe consequences when safe-to-run. Use two independent adjudicators (predefined adjudication protocol) to label ambiguous cases; report inter-rater agreement. Predefine adversarial construction rules, policy definitions for 'unsafe', and adjudication/tie-breaker rules; preregister the plan.
candidates.expected_data: Per-prompt records: prompt text, LLM output, mitigation condition, mitigation accept/reject, verifier detection flags, adjudicator labels (unsafe/safe/ambiguous), emulator deployment result for accepted outputs (if executed), time-to-detection, and bypass case transcripts.
candidates.primary_outcome: Mitigation detection effectiveness: proportion of adversarial unsafe outputs blocked by verifier+policy gating versus no-mitigation baseline (precision, recall, and F1 relative to adjudicated ground truth).
candidates.analysis_outline: Compute detection rates, false-positive and false-negative rates per mitigation arm; compare proportions with chi-squared or Fisher exact tests. Calculate precision, recall, and F1 for each mitigation strategy relative to adjudicated labels. Report inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa). Analyze adversarial examples that bypassed mitigation to characterize failure modes and recommend policy enhancements; include qualitative transcripts.
risks: Adversarial prompt construction may produce ethically sensitive or potentially harmful content; experiments limited to emulator-only and safe-adversarial protocols.
Adjudication of 'unsafe' can be subjective; require dual adjudicators and tie-breaker rules to reduce bias.
Tested mitigations are prototypical and may not reflect production-grade defense effectiveness, limiting generalizability.

candidates.title: Constrained Decoding and Live Schema-Grounding to Reduce Semantic/Execution Failures
candidates.research_question: To what extent do constrained decoding and live schema-grounding (schema-aware token constraints and retrieval of device-specific schemas) reduce semantic and execution failures in LLM-generated network configurations compared with unconstrained generation and RAG-only approaches?
hypotheses: Constrained decoding combined with live schema-grounding will yield lower verifier-failure and emulator-execution-failure rates than unconstrained LLM generation.
Schema-grounding tailored to device/vendor CLI dialects will reduce vendor-specific semantic errors more than generic constrained decoding alone.
Constrained decoding may increase refusal or partial-output rates, trading off coverage for correctness in some classes of intents.
candidates.proposed_design: Assemble n=200 intent tasks spanning vendor-like CLI dialects and change types. Evaluate four generation conditions per intent: (A) unconstrained LLM, (B) LLM with constrained decoding (token-level schema constraints), (C) RAG retrieval of device schemas + LLM, (D) constrained decoding + live schema-grounding (both). For each output run deterministic verification and emulate accepted outputs. Predefine constrained-decode grammars and schema-retrieval rules, and preregister refusal handling and retry rules. Record verifier and emulator outcomes, refusal rates, and time/latency metrics.
candidates.expected_data: Per-intent and per-condition records: intent, generated config, constrained-decoding flags, retrieved schema snippets (if any), verifier result, emulator execution logs, refusal/partial-output flags, execution errors, and vendor-dialect mismatch notes.
candidates.primary_outcome: Reduction in combined verifier-failure + emulator-execution-failure rate for constrained-decoding + schema-grounding condition relative to unconstrained baseline (absolute and relative reductions).
candidates.analysis_outline: Compute and compare failure proportions across the four conditions using repeated-measures tests (McNemar for paired binary outcomes or Cochran's Q for multi-condition comparison). Report per-intent paired differences with 95% CIs. Fit mixed-effects logistic regression with random intercepts for intent and fixed effects for condition, intent complexity, and vendor dialect. Report refusal rates and analyze correctness/coverage trade-offs qualitatively and quantitatively.
risks: Constrained decoding may cause increased refusals or truncated outputs, reducing usable coverage for some intents.
Maintaining up-to-date device-specific schemas may be challenging; schema mismatch can create false negatives.
Schema-grounding and constrained decoding introduce latency and engineering complexity that may limit operational practicality.
